primitives.name: Vulnerability Reporting Process
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Security Policy ## Reporting a Vulnerability Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.
primitives.assumptions: Vulnerabilities are stochastic events requiring private communication channels.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Public disclosure leads to information leakage and exploitability.

layer2.mapping: The reporting process mirrors Bayesian updating where prior knowledge is refined upon receipt of new evidence (vulnerability report).
layer2.telemetry: Time between report submission and patch release indicates response efficiency.

primitives.name: Supported Versions Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Supported Versions Security fixes are focused on the latest published 0.x version and the current development branch.
primitives.assumptions: Only active software versions receive security patches.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Outdated versions become attack vectors post-patch release.

layer2.mapping: Version support defines a kernel of acceptable risk; older versions lie outside this kernel and are subject to increased exposure.
layer2.telemetry: Number of patched vs. unpatched installations reflects compliance and exposure metrics.

primitives.name: Private Disclosure Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: We will review reports and coordinate fixes before public disclosure.
primitives.assumptions: Coordination delays reduce immediate exploitation window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure to coordinate results in premature disclosure and widespread compromise.

layer2.mapping: Private disclosure resembles a controlled experiment where variables (vulnerabilities) are isolated until validated and mitigated.
layer2.telemetry: Average time from report to patch deployment measures protocol efficacy.

The reporting mechanism enforces a private channel to prevent information cascades that could enable exploitation. This aligns with Bayesian inference principles where initial uncertainty (unknown vulnerabilities) is reduced via empirical evidence (reports). The supported versions constraint introduces a discrete state space where only certain configurations are considered secure, effectively defining a kernel of operational safety. The private disclosure protocol acts as a temporal gatekeeper, delaying public exposure until mitigation strategies are deployed. These primitives form a dualistic framework: one side governs the probabilistic nature of threats, while the other manages their deterministic resolution within defined boundaries.
